source.title_on_document: Exploring the Potential of Metacognitive Support Agents for Human-AI Co-Creation

supplement.where: The paper refers to 'the video figure in the supplementary material' (p. 9, Section 5.5.2), an external example summary video. Appendix A is inside this PDF (pp. 21–26) and contains participant and wizard demographics, interaction timelines, wizard guidelines and agent introductions, the HephAIstus project planning sheet, a sketching-board example, and the interview protocol. The planning sheet (p. 24, Section A.1.4) is not a separate task design brief.
supplement.holds: A video figure with an example summary video. No statistics are said to sit only in the supplement.

paper_design_summary: Twenty mechanical designers used the Generative Design extension of Autodesk Fusion360 to design a ship engine mounting bracket while thinking aloud. Five designers each worked with one of three voice support agents that humans operated in a Wizard-of-Oz setup (SocratAIs, HephAIstus, Expert-Freeform), and five worked with no support; the paper does not say how designers were assigned to groups. The researchers scored each final design from 1 to 5 on five feasibility criteria and analyzed think-aloud videos and interviews qualitatively.

studies.label: Wizard-of-Oz study of metacognitive support agents (engine bracket design)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Support condition: one of three human-operated voice support agent probes (SocratAIs, HephAIstus, Expert-Freeform) or no support; every participant used the Fusion360 Generative Design tool. The method of assignment is not stated.
assignment.quote: we conducted a formative between-subjects study with trained mechanical designers new to working with generative AI. Each designer was supported by a different agent probe (facilitated by a human operator in the background)
assignment.locator: p. 6, Section 5 (Study Design); p. 2, Section 1 ('one agent probe (or received no support in a control condition)')

arms.name: SocratAIs
arms.description: Generative Design tool plus a voice agent, operated by the first author, that asked reflective questions and replied to user requests only with questions

arms.name: HephAIstus
arms.description: Generative Design tool plus a voice agent, operated by the first author, that prompted planning and free-body-diagram sketching, gave proactive suggestions, and answered user questions

arms.name: Expert-Freeform
arms.description: Generative Design tool plus a voice agent operated by an external Autodesk Generative Design expert, who supported the designer in their preferred way without directly instructing them

arms.name: No Support
arms.description: Generative Design tool with no support agent

participants.exclusions: None reported: 'All participants completed the task without abandoning it' (p. 9, Section 6). Table 2 lists 5 participants per group.
participants.who: Designers aged 20 to 42 with mechanical engineering backgrounds and at least two years of CAD and Fusion360 experience but no experience with the Generative Design extension; a mix of undergraduates, graduate students, and professional engineers, paid 20 USD per hour
participants.country: Not stated; recruited from engineering departments of North American universities and through the Upwork platform
participants.quote: We recruited 20 designers (aged 20 to 42 (M = 26.1, SD = 5.9)) with mechanical engineering backgrounds from engineering departments of North American universities and through the Upwork freelance hiring platform
participants.locator: p. 7, Section 5.1 (Participants); p. 10, Table 2 and Figure 3 (n = 5 per group)

ai_tool.name_model: Autodesk Fusion360 'Generative Design' extension (all arms); voice support agents simulated by human wizards, with speech generated by Google's text-to-speech API from wizard-typed text
ai_tool.how_used: All designers specified loads, constraints, and obstacle geometry for the Generative Design solver, which generated about 20 candidate designs. In the three support arms a human wizard, presented to the designer as an AI agent, sent voice messages while watching the designer's screen and think-aloud; participants were debriefed afterward that humans had controlled the agents.

task.description: Design a light and strong ship engine mounting bracket with Fusion360 Generative Design from a design brief and starter file; participants then chose three feasible generated parts, and the highest-scoring part became the final design.
task.duration: Onboarding 30 minutes; design task part 1 up to 70 minutes, 30-minute solver break, part 2 up to 30 minutes; participants worked between 31 and 99 minutes

outcomes.name: Design outcome quality score (feasibility, 1 to 5)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: The researchers checked the final bracket against the design brief on five criteria, one point each: passing finite element analysis, feasible load case setup, mass optimized, feasible fastener clearance, part fits the bounding dimensions. Per-criterion checkmarks are in Table 2.

contrasts.treatment_arm: Agent-supported groups pooled (SocratAIs, HephAIstus, Expert-Freeform; n = 15)
contrasts.reported: Supported M = 3.5 (SD = 1.4) vs No Support M = 1.0 (SD = 0.0). Group means (Table 2, Figure 3): SocratAIs 4.0 (n = 5), HephAIstus 3.2 (n = 5), Expert-Freeform 3.4 (n = 5), No Support 1 (n = 5). No statistical test reported; 'the small sample size per group prevents us from drawing conclusions about statistically significant differences between the support conditions'.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Section 6.1.1; p. 10, Table 2, Figure 3, and text

company_involvement.description: Coauthor Ye Wang is affiliated with Autodesk Research. Autodesk employees were recruited via internal mailing lists and snowball sampling to operate the Expert-Freeform support agents.
company_involvement.locator: PDF p. 1, author affiliations (Ye Wang, Autodesk Research); p. 6, Section 4.3; p. 21, Appendix A, Table 5.

eligibility.reason: Criterion 1 is not met: the contrast varies human-operated metacognitive support while all groups use the same Fusion360 Generative Design tool; no implemented generative-AI assistance or configuration is varied, and random assignment is not reported (p. 2, Section 1; pp. 6–8, Sections 4.3–5.4). Criterion 2 is not met: 20 people were analyzed, five per group (p. 7, Section 5.1; p. 9, Section 6; p. 10, Table 2 and Figure 3). Criterion 3 is met: submitted designs were scored on a five-criterion feasibility rubric, which falls under usefulness for a design task (p. 9, Section 5.5.1; creativity-codebook.md Sections 1, 3, and 6). Core remains no. No listed context class applies to this human-support comparison within a common AI-assisted task, so context_class remains none.

one_line_finding: Designers supported by a Wizard-of-Oz agent scored M = 3.5 (SD = 1.4, n = 15) on a 1-to-5 design feasibility score versus M = 1.0 (SD = 0.0, n = 5) without support, with no statistical test (p. 9, Section 6.1.1; p. 10, Table 2).

Criterion 3 is unclear: the only output score is a feasibility rubric for an engineering part, not a creativity or diversity rating. The paper belongs in the screening report as a small experiment.
